answer.evidence: The top of the building is a large horizontal area seen from above in rows 0-33. It has brick wall-top rims (rows 0-4), a charred floor visible inside the open north half (rows 5-19, evidence d), and the grey upper slab (rows 20-29). The slab ends in a broken brick edge and a dark front-edge line at row 34, followed by dark eave shadow in rows 35-36. Below that, the soot-blackened brick front face runs from row 35 to row 95 (about 61 rows) with two rows of window holes and a ledge line at rows 64-65. This gives a top surface plus a tall front face, so the drawing reads as three-quarter view.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has 11 visible tones per tile against 12 and 10 for the references, so it matches them on density. Near-flat coverage is 10% against 0%, which is a small amount of flat fill, probably in the dark window holes and parts of the slab. Only 11% of its dark edge pixels are neutral (references 7% and 9%), so the outlines lean brown or red-brown, in the dark tone of the adjacent material, and are not a black sticker line. By eye, the brick wall is mottled with several red-brown steps and per-brick variation. The floor slab and charred debris add grey and brown clusters, and the window holes carry dark soot detail. The brick ramp has about 4 steps, a little under the references' 5-6. The raw total of 23 colours is much lower than the references, but that follows from the locked palette and the primary visible-tone facts are on par. A careful artist would accept it next to the references, though it is slightly simpler than them.

Below that is a soot-blackened brick front face of about 65 rows (rows 31-95) with two rows of window holes and a doorway. The top surface is clearly foreshortened above the vertical front face, so it reads as a 3/4 view.

styleAnswer.evidence: Measured facts are close to the references: 11 visible tones per tile against 12 and 10, 10% near-flat coverage against 0%, and only 11% neutral dark edge pixels, so the outlines lean brown or blue-black rather than neutral black. By eye, the brick facade has a few red-brown steps with scattered brick-course texture, and the charred windows are dark blue-brown. The upper slab and burnt interior are mostly 3-4 dark tones with sparse debris dots. The candidate has only 23 distinct colours in total against 66 and 185 in the references, so its ramps are shallower. Each material shows about 4 steps against the references' 5-6, and the brick and slab areas are somewhat flat and repetitive. There are no per-brick highlights like the references' per-tile scallops and stone-by-stone shading. It is an acceptable ruin, but it is thinner than the references in shading depth and variety, and when in doubt this fails.
